glossary.definition: (A) "Atomic energy" means all forms of energy released in the course of nuclear fission or nuclear transformation.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (B) "By-product material" has the same meaning as in section 3748.01 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (C) "Production facility" means any equipment or device capable of the production of special nuclear material in such quantity as to be of significance to the common defense and security, or in such manner as to affect the health and safety of the public; or any important component part especially designed for such equipment or device.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (D) "Special nuclear material" has the same meaning as in section 3748.01 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (E) "Utilization facility" means any equipment or device, except an atomic weapon, capable of making use of special nuclear materials in such quantity as to be of significance to the common defense and security, or in such manner as to affect the health and safety of the public, or peculiarly adapted for making use of atomic energy in such quantity as to be of significance to the common defense and security, or in such manner as to affect the health and safety of the public; or any important component part especially designed for such equipment or device.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (F) "Radiation" has the same meaning as in section 3748.01 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (G) "Highway route controlled quantity" has the same meaning as in 49 C.F.R. 173.403.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:
As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (I) "Spent nuclear fuel" means fuel that has been withdrawn from a nuclear reactor following irradiation, the constituent elements of which have not been separated by reprocessing.
glossary.scope: As used in Chapter 4163. of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (J) "Transuranic waste" means material contaminated with elements that have an atomic number greater than ninety-two, including neptunium, plutonium, americium, and curium, and that are in concentrations greater than ten nanocuries per gram or in other concentrations that the United States nuclear regulatory commission may prescribe.
